chunk_findings.detail: `review_threads` commits the forge mutations before it has a report it can stand behind, and any failure after the first mutation is reported as a failure of the whole call. Concretely: for a PR whose thread `T` exists, run `pr threads <id> --thread T --reply "Addressed in abc123" --resolve`. `forge.reply(...)` posts the comment and sets `rep.replied = True`; then (a) if `forge.resolve(...)` raises `ForgeError`, the handler returns a report whose `refused` is non-empty while the reply is already public and `rep.threads` was never refreshed, or (b) if both mutations succeed but the follow-up `found = forge.threads(it.pr.number)` raises `ForgeUnavailable`, the call returns with `unavailable` set even though both writes landed. In either case the only error-shaped fields the caller has (`refused`/`unavailable`) say the operation did not complete, while the reply — which is not idempotent — has already been posted; an operator (or any caller that keys success off the error fields rather than `rep.replied`/`rep.resolved`) that retries will post the identical reply a second time on the thread. Ordering/atomicity should be resolved (e.g., verify the re-read/report path, or make the reply idempotent / surface the partial state as success-with-warning) so a transient failure after a committed write cannot be presented as a plain failure.

chunk_findings.detail: The mutation branch mutates the in-memory state (`thread["resolved"] = True`, or `thread["comments"].append(...)`) and returns `{"data": {"ok": True}}` without ever calling `_save(self.path, st)`, even though every other state-changing helper in this file does (e.g. the newly added `add_thread` calls `_save(self.path, st)` at the end, and `queue_land` does too). Since fakeforge is a CLI shim that reads its state (`st`) from `self.path` at startup and persists it back only via `_save`, the resolution/reply is discarded when the process exits. Concretely: after `fake.add_thread(1, "T1", "why?")`, running the CLI `pr threads 1 --thread T1 --resolve` and then running `pr threads 1` again (a fresh fakeforge process, reading the same JSON file) still reports the thread as unresolved, and `fake.thread(1, "T1")["resolved"]` likewise stays `False`; the same applies to replies made with `--reply`, whose appended comment never lands in the file. The fix is to call `_save(self.path, st)` before `return done(out=json.dumps({"data": {"ok": True}}))`.

chunk_findings.detail: The `_GH_THREADS_QUERY` string literal is not brace-balanced. Tracking the selection sets: `repository`, `pullRequest`, `reviewThreads`, `reviewThreads.nodes`, `nodes.comments`, `comments.nodes`, and `author` are opened (seven `{`), and `author{login}` is closed inline, so the document must end with exactly six closing braces after `body` (`...{login} body}}}}}}`). The literal instead ends `...{login} body}}}}}}}` — seven trailing `}` for six outstanding selection sets. That extra `}` is a parse error, so `gh api graphql` returns an `errors` payload rather than data; `GitHub.threads()` reaches `if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("errors"):` and raises `ForgeError("review threads of #N: Syntax Error: Expected Name, found \"}\" ...")`. Every call path that depends on this method — CLI `pr threads <id>`, `services.flow.review_threads`, `api.pr_threads`, and MCP `ddflow_pr_threads` — therefore fails on every PR, while the fakeforge-backed tests never detect it because they do not execute this real query.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/forge.py:_GH_THREADS_QUERY

chunk_findings.detail:
The fake never strips a query string off the endpoint before tokenizing it, even though the `fields` comprehension on the previous line (`... and not a.startswith("projects")`) only makes sense if an argument beginning with `projects` can contain an `=`, i.e. the adapter is expected to pass endpoints of the form `projects/.../discussions...?<param>=<value>`. With such an endpoint the two lines disagree:

- `endpoint = "projects/7/merge_requests/3/discussions?per_page=100"` → `parts` contains `"discussions?per_page=100"`, so `"discussions" not in parts` is true and the fake exits 2 ("unsupported"), even though a plain discussion listing was requested.
- `endpoint = "projects/7/merge_requests/3/discussions/abc?resolved=true"` (the documented GitLab resolve URL) → `parts` contains `"discussions"`, but `rest[0] == "abc?resolved=true"`, which never equals `d["id"]`, so `disc is None` and the fake returns a 404 instead of resolving the thread.

So any adapter call that carries its parameters in the URL — the canonical GitLab form for `PUT .../discussions/:id?resolved=true`, and the normal form for paginated listings — is mishandled by the same fake that was written to accept it. The fix is to split the query off `endpoint` (or compare against the id before the `?`) before building `parts`/`rest`.
